title: Physical activity care situation in acute geriatric care units - a cross-sectional study
summary: Patients spend most of their hospital stay in bed or sitting up. Their state of health or the reason for their hospitalisation is irrelevant. Too little physical activity has negative health consequences even after a short time, such as a decrease in strength and mobility, a longer hospital stay or a higher risk of death. Promoting physical activity has a positive effect on health and can improve quality of life. Therefore, the aim of this study is to investigate how much patients on geriatric hospital wards move and what factors influence this from the perspective of patients, their relatives and hospital staff. This information will be collected using various methods. Movement behaviour is recorded using so-called activity trackers, which are attached to the patient's ankle. Influencing factors will be collected either through questionnaires, interviews or the so-called photovoice method. In the latter, photos will be taken by the three interest groups, which will then be analysed together with the study staff.
conditions: In the present study, all patients on an acute geriatric ward, regardless of their diagnosis, are considered in the context of care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The subjects of the study consist of 3 groups (patients, interprofessional carers, relatives) in the  acute geriatric care units, for which different inclusion criteria are defined.

a. The following inclusion criteria apply to the ‘patients’ group
- Age ≥ 65 years,
- Stay in one of the two cooperating wards that lasted of at least 3 days
- No absolute contraindications for exercise or training,
- Sufficient German language skills to understand verbal and written instructions

b. The following inclusion criteria apply to the group ‘interprofessional carers’:
- Age ≥ 18 years,
- Successfully completed training/studies in the healthcare sector, e.g., doctor, nursing, occupational/physical/sports therapy, social work,
- Have worked on one of the co-operating wards for at least 1 year,
- Weekly working hours: at least 50% of a full-time position,
- On average, at least 50% of the weekly working hours contain day shifts (between 6:00 am and 10:00 pm) and at least 2 days / week,
- At least 3 years of professional experience in internal medicine or geriatrics
- Sufficient German language skills to understand verbal and written instructions.

c. The following inclusion criteria apply to the ‘Relatives’ group:
- Age ≥ 18 years,
- A person who describes themselves as a relative of a patient on the cooperating wards. This means that this person takes care of the patient both in their private life and during their hospitalisation.
- Sufficient German language skills to understand verbal and written instructions.
Exclusion criteria:
None or not meeting the inclusion criteria.
